spp_hugo_guide.text: Victor Hugo bought this house in 1856 and decorated every inch of it, with carved oak, old tiles, tapestries and furniture he had designed himself. The Hauteville House of today is a work of art made by a writer.
At the top is the Look-Out, a glass room with a view over the harbour all the way to France. Hugo wrote standing up at a desk there, and gazed out across the sea to the country that had exiled him.

spp_hugo_study.text: Much of Les Misérables was written here, and it was published in 1862 while he still lived on Guernsey. He wrote Toilers of the Sea here, too. It features an octopus, which gave the French a whole new nightmare.
Hugo's exile ended in 1870 when Napoleon III fell, and he went home to Paris a hero. He came back to Guernsey for a time, too. He loved these islands.
